correctness.rationale: Fixed N and P give exactly (P−1)(N−P−1) positive-cell matrices with free TP and FP. Independently enumerated every pair at every P for N=4,5,6,7: matrix totals 1,4,10,20, within-prevalence pairs 0,2,12,42, and exactly 0,0,0,3 strict reversals, with all three claimed N=7 pairs reproduced. For witness A=(2,1,2,2), B=(3,2,1,1), F1 increases 4/7 to 2/3 while MCC decreases 1/6 to 1/sqrt(120), both positive. Independently symbolically factored odd/even infinite families: F1 differences 6/[(2k+7)(2k+9)] and 6/[(2k+9)(2k+11)]; positive squared-MCC cross products (k+3)(k+4)(2k+7)(3k²+11k+4) and 4(k+3)(k+4)²(k+5)(3k+2). Thus every N>=7 has an exact reversal. Positive-cell and same prevalence boundaries are essential.
residual_risks: The threshold is under all-positive-cells and fixed actual P, not arbitrary classifiers or confidence intervals.

originality.rationale: The 2020 Chicco–Jurman full open-access article examines discrepancies between F1 and MCC on six synthetic scenarios and genomics data, showing general disagreement. Its methods and case-study sections do not state a least integer N under both strict positivity and common prevalence; indexed text searches for seven and fixed prevalence found no matches. The accepted novelty scope excludes the well-known existence of reversal: it is the sharp 7-case threshold, three complete minimum-layer pairs and for-all-N construction. Resultary semantic search did not identify the same finite threshold; folklore exercise risk remains.

value.rationale: Classifier scores can disagree even on the same sample with identical actual class prevalence. The sharp seven-observation boundary and exact first layer isolate how small the disagreement can be under nondegenerate confusion matrices. The all-larger-size positive-MCC reversal construction prevents this from being a purely artificial N=7 curiosity. It is a motivated finite cutoff for two widespread metrics, not a new evaluation metric or a claim of empirical reliability.
